subject: Longitudinal CFA: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite

messages.author: b430763ad49e6cd0
messages.subject: Longitudinal CFA: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite
parts:
Dear all,

In a first phase I modeled separate one-factor CFAs for every time point (4 in total). At first independently, in the sense that at each time point I would reduce the measurement model as much as possible until a good model fit was established (based on several overall fit indices, residual correlations and reliability). Then I tried e.g. the model from time = 1 on the remaining three time points and repeated this for the other ones too. This way I now have a model that fits well at all time points (rsmea < .06, cfi > .96, tli > .96, pvalue > 0.05, srmr < .08). Cronbach's alpha was between 0.7 and 0.8 for all time points. 

I wanted to continue the analysis by doing a longitudinal CFA. I fit the above configuration as follows:

Model0 <- ' Factor1 =~ MV1_1 + MV1_2 + MV1_3 + MV1_4
                   Factor2 =~ MV2_1 + MV2_2 + MV2_3 + MV2_4
                   Factor3 =~ MV3_1 + MV3_2 + MV3_3 + MV3_4
                   Factor4=~  MV4_1 + MV4_2 + MV4_3 + MV4_4  '

where the first number indicates the time point (1, 2, 3, 4) and the second indicates the n'th item (1, 2, 3, 4)

For all these items I allowed covariance between time points, such that item 1 would correlate with itself (i.e. MV1_1 ~~ MV2_2, MV2_2 ~~ MV3_3, MV3_3~~ MV4_4)

I also allowed for covariance between the factors, i.e.:

            Factor1 ~~ Factor2 + Factor3 + Factor4 
            Factor2 ~~ Factor3 + Factor4
            Factor3 ~~ Factor4

I fit this model with the above mentioned covariances using: lavaan( model = model, data = data, auto.var = TRUE)

Upon fitting this model, I get the warning message: In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite;

I understand from an earlier post, answered by Yves Rosseel, what this means: the factors are (almost) indistinguishable. The standardized estimates for their covariances range from 0.936 to 1.014, which seem high. See below. 











I was wondering two things:
1) Am I right that this is normal / expected to occur in Longitudinal CFA? As the four factors are the same, except that they are measured at a different moment in time. 
2) Is this a problem for my analysis? And if so, what could or should I do about it? 

Thanks a lot for your efforts and help in advance.

Best,
Amonet

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal CFA: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite
parts: I believe the problem is that some correlations are > 1. Is there a way for me to tell lavaan it must be 0.99 at most for example?

That is not advisable:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.13.2.150

Instead, you can simply look at the 95% CI for the factor correlations, and check that the interval contains admissible values.  If so, then the out-of-bounds estimate is consistent with sampling error:

http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0049124112442138

Note, however, that model misspecification is also a potential cause of out-of-bounds estimates.  So if your model fit statistic is significant, then you have evidence against the null hypothesis of perfect fit, in which case you also need to consider model misspecification as the cause.  But if the model misfit is not very bad (e.g., correlation residuals are all within +/- 0.10), then minor misspecification is probably not a serious contender as the cause of an out-of-bounds value.

resid(fit0, type = "cor")

Your residual correlations are incorrectly specified, and you also need to estimate residual covariances among the same items measured on non-consecutive occasions.

## item 1
MV1_1 ~~ MV2_1 + MV3_1 + MV4_1
MV2_1 ~~ MV3_1 + MV4_1
MV3_1 ~~ MV4_1

## item 2
MV1_2 ~~ MV2_2 + MV3_2 + MV4_2
MV2_2 ~~ MV3_2 + MV4_2
...

Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

parts:
I was wondering two more things I came across, but haven't found any literature about: insignificant error variances of items. In my preliminary analysis of 1-factor models on 1 time point and 2-factor models on 1 time point, insignificant error variances sometimes occurred. Are these also Heywood cases in the sense that the model is possibly incorrectly specified? 

In my longitudinal CFA model several insignificant error covariances pop up (between time points of the same item). Does this work similarly as to insignificant items' factor loadings? Such that I should remove insignificant terms from my model 1 by 1 or altogether? 

Thanks,

Amonet.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal CFA: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite
parts: insignificant error variances sometimes occurred. Are these also Heywood cases in the sense that the model is possibly incorrectly specified?

No.  A negative estimated (residual) variance is a Heywood case.  But following the same principles I described for out-of-bounds correlations, if the negative variance estimate is not significant (because its 95% CI includes positive values), then it is consistent with sampling error.
In my longitudinal CFA model several insignificant error covariances pop up (between time points of the same item).

You leave residual covariances in the model regardless of whether they happen to be significant in your particular sample.  Statistical significance is a function of sample size as well as effect size.  The estimate might be small, but it is still theoretically meaningful (there is item-specific variance that re-occurs each time the same item is administered).
Does this work similarly as to insignificant items' factor loadings? Such that I should remove insignificant terms from my model 1 by 1 or altogether?
